title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Get Portal Pods
content: Pokémon Pokopia added Portal Pods with its 2.0.0 update, and they solve one of the game's most persistent headaches: running out of accessible storage mid-session. Think of them as the Pokopia equivalent of Minecraft's Ender Chest. Each Portal Pod holds up to 140 stacks of items, and any Portal Pod you interact with anywhere in the world taps into that same shared inventory. Place one at your base, one in the field, and your items follow you everywhere. There are two ways to get one: find the free copy hidden in Bubbly Basin, or unlock the crafting recipe by progressing through Palette Town. Here's exactly how both work. Portal Pod holds 140 item stacks Where to find the free Portal Pod in Bubbly Basin The quickest way to get your first Portal Pod requires the Expansion Pass and access to Bubbly Basin . If you have both, this is the route to take before spending anything on crafting. From the Bubbly Basin entrance, move past the opening area where Popplio first guides you. Rather than swimming underwater the whole way, use Surf to travel above the water 's surface. Head past the ornate building that pokes above the waterline, and aim for the island directly behind it. tip Navigating above water with Surf is faster than diving through the underwater sections. Save the diving for when you reach the island. Once you reach that island, dive beneath the surface and enter the building. Inside, you'll find a Portal Pod that can be collected using Rock Smash . There's a second one at the bottom of the stairs at the back of the building, sitting inside a Poké Ball. That gives you two Portal Pods from a single trip. How to get more Portal Pods after the first two Two Portal Pods is a solid start, but you'll likely want more as your base and travel routes expand. There are two methods to duplicate them without crafting. First, once you have a Portal Pod in hand, head to the 3D printer inside a rebuilt Pokémon Center . Take a picture of the Portal Pod, and you can print as many copies as you want from that point forward. If you haven't rebuilt yours yet, check out the Pokémon Pokopia guide on rebuilding the Pokémon Center to get that structure up and running. Second, if a friend has a Portal Pod on their island, you can travel there and photograph theirs instead. The same applies to any Cloud Island you visit. Either way, the photo is what unlocks the print option, so the source doesn't matter. important The 3D printer method only works after the Pokémon Center has been rebuilt. If yours isn't ready yet, the Bubbly Basin find is your only immediate option. How to unlock the Portal Pod crafting recipe Crafting a Portal Pod from scratch is the alternative path, and it doesn't require the Expansion Pass. The catch is that it takes longer to unlock. Palette Town is where the recipe comes from. This separate area functions as a blank building canvas where you can encounter Pokémon not found in the four main towns or in Bubbly Basin. As you build and develop Palette Town, your environment level increases, and leveling it up enough after the 2.0.0 update rewards you with the Portal Pod recipe. Loading table... The crafting route is described as the cheapest option long-term since you skip the 3D printer 's material costs entirely. If you're patient and already working through Palette Town progression, it's worth holding out for the recipe rather than spending resources on printing. warning Don't assume the crafting recipe is available from the start of Palette Town. You need to reach a specific environment level threshold, so build consistently and check your rewards as you progress. Palette Town unlocks the recipe What makes Portal Pods worth the effort? The 140-stack shared inventory is the headline, but the real value is the flexibility. Once you have Portal Pods placed at multiple locations, you stop making trips back to base just to deposit materials. Combined with smart fast travel options in Pokémon Pokopia , Portal Pods cut out a significant chunk of the back-and-forth that slows down building sessions. For players deep into crafting, having access to your full material stockpile from anywhere on the island changes how you plan builds. You can gather resources in one area and immediately start constructing in another without ever unloading at a chest first. Place Portal Pods at every base If you're still building out your island and figuring out which materials to prioritize, the best items to buy first in Pokémon Pokopia is a good starting point before committing your resources. For everything else the game has to offer, the full Pokémon Pokopia strategy guides collection covers crafting, building, and exploration in detail.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Get Shiny Pearls in Bubbly Basin
content: Shiny Pearls are one of the most-needed resources in Pokémon Pokopia 's Bubbly Basin expansion, and the game does a poor job of telling you how to actually get them. You won't find them sitting on the ocean floor. Getting them requires a specific Pokémon ability, and if you don't know which one, you'll be sitting on a pile of useless Grubby Pearls wondering what went wrong. What are Shiny Pearls and why do you need them? Shiny Pearls are a refined material used in a wide range of crafting recipes and Pokémon requests throughout Bubbly Basin. As you rebuild Cerulean City, demand for Shiny Pearls ramps up fast, and running dry on them will stall your progress significantly. The raw form , Grubby Pearls , are plentiful in Bubbly Basin and easy to collect. The problem is they have zero direct use on their own. Every Grubby Pearl needs to be converted into a Shiny Pearl before it becomes useful, and that conversion process is the part most players miss. Grubby Pearls before conversion How do you get Shiny Pearls in Pokémon Pokopia? Shiny Pearls cannot be found directly in the overworld. The only way to produce them is by assigning a Pokémon with the Scrub specialty to process your Grubby Pearls. Without a Scrub Pokémon in your setup, those Grubby Pearls will sit in your inventory forever. The first time most players encounter this mechanic is through a request from Mareanie , who asks for a Shiny Pearl. That request effectively serves as the game's tutorial for the system, pointing you toward Cloyster as the most accessible Scrub Pokémon at that stage. tip Check your active requests regularly. Mareanie 's Shiny Pearl request is the clearest early-game signal that you need to set up a Scrub Pokémon as soon as possible. How to get for the Scrub specialty Cloyster is the easiest entry point for the Scrub specialty in Bubbly Basin. It spawns from the Swaying Flower Bed & Seaweed Habitat , which you can build yourself once you know the recipe. The habitat requires: 4x Seabad Flowers 1x Chimney Rock 2x Lush Seaweed Once the habitat is placed and Cloyster spawns, you can assign it to process Grubby Pearls into Shiny Pearls. The habitat requirements are revealed as part of Mareanie 's request, so following that quest line is the most natural path to unlocking this conversion chain. Cloyster habitat build requirements All Pokémon with the Scrub specialty Cloyster isn't the only option. Two other Pokémon also carry the Scrub specialty, and running multiple Scrub Pokémon simultaneously is the fastest way to process a large Grubby Pearl backlog. Loading table... Splitting a large stack of Grubby Pearls across Cloyster , Shellder , and Sharpedo at the same time cuts down the wait considerably compared to routing everything through a single Pokémon. warning Don't let Grubby Pearls pile up without a Scrub Pokémon assigned. A large backlog takes time to clear, and many crafting recipes and requests will be blocked until you have enough Shiny Pearls converted. Tips for keeping your Shiny Pearl supply healthy The crafting demand for Shiny Pearls in Bubbly Basin is consistent enough that running out is a genuine problem if you're not proactive. A few habits that help: Keep track of where your Scrub Pokémon are located at all times so you can assign them quickly when a batch of Grubby Pearls comes in. Build multiple Scrub-compatible habitats if you want a faster pipeline. Having Shellder and Sharpedo alongside Cloyster means you're never bottlenecked by a single Pokémon. Prioritize Grubby Pearl collection during your regular Bubbly Basin sessions so your Scrub Pokémon always have material to work with. tip Grubby Pearls are found throughout Bubbly Basin and are one of the more common drops in the area, so supply on the raw material side shouldn't be the problem. The conversion rate is the bottleneck. Assigning Cloyster to Scrub tasks What else should you know about Bubbly Basin? Shiny Pearls are just one piece of the Bubbly Basin resource puzzle. The underwater area introduced with the Expansion Pass brings a lot of new systems, habitats, and Pokémon that interact in ways that aren't always obvious. If you're still getting started with the DLC, the guide on how to unlock Bubbly Basin covers the prerequisites and how to find the underwater gate. title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Learn Suck and Move Water
content: If you have been trying to move water around in Pokémon Pokopia and keep hitting a wall, you are not alone. The Suck move is one of Ditto 's most useful abilities in the game, letting you vacuum up bodies of water and deposit them exactly where you want. But unlocking it requires working through a specific chain of story events that the game does not spell out clearly. Here is everything you need to know to get Suck and start reshaping your island's waterways. What Does the Suck Move Actually Do? Suck functions like a water bucket in sandbox games such as Minecraft . It allows Ditto to inhale a block of liquid and carry it until you choose to release it somewhere else. According to game guides, the move works on a wide range of liquids including water , ocean water , hot-spring water , vending machine drinks , and even lava . This makes it one of the most flexible tools in Pokémon Pokopia for island customization. You can use it to: Clear flooded areas that are blocking habitats Construct custom ponds, creeks, or rivers from scratch Redirect water sources to attract water -type Pokémon Build hot springs or lava features for specific habitat requirements Ditto 's Suck move in action warning Spitting liquid onto an area that is not enclosed by blocks will cause it to spread unevenly. This can accidentally flood nearby habitats, so always prepare a contained pool before releasing liquid. How to Unlock the Suck Move Unlocking Suck is tied to a specific questline and cannot be obtained by exploring freely. You need to follow the story progression carefully across two separate areas. Step 1: Rebuild the Rocky Ridges Pokémon Center Before anything else, you must advance far enough through the Rocky Ridges area to rebuild the Pokémon Center there. This is a major milestone that sits at the end of a series of smaller quests and tasks in that zone. Expect to spend a significant amount of time completing those prerequisite requests before the center becomes available. As confirmed by community discussion on Reddit and summarized across multiple guides, the Rocky Ridges Pokémon Center rebuild is the key gate that unlocks the next step in the chain. Step 2: Talk to Piplup at Bleak Beach Once the Rocky Ridges Pokémon Center is rebuilt, head to Bleak Beach and speak directly with Piplup . This step is easy to miss because the request does not appear in your request list automatically. You must physically talk to Piplup to trigger the Make a Waterfall request. danger Do not wait for this quest to appear on its own. It only activates after a direct conversation with Piplup , so make the trip to Bleak Beach as soon as the Pokémon Center is done. Step 3: Create a Marshy Tall Grass Habitat Piplup 's waterfall request requires the help of Paldean Wooper , who you need to attract to your island. To do this, you must build a marshy tall grass habitat. According to Game8's walkthrough team, this habitat requires placing 4 yellow tall grass tiles adjacent to a body of muddy water . A waterfall of muddy water can be found southwest of the Withered Wasteland gate if you need a source. Once you place the habitat components correctly, wait for Paldean Wooper to arrive. After it shows up and you complete the interaction, Ditto will learn the Suck move. How to Use Suck: Full Controls Once Ditto has learned Suck , using it is straightforward once you understand the button layout. Here is a full breakdown of the controls: Action Button Input Inhale liquid Hold Y + ZR while facing the liquid Spit out liquid Press A while facing target area Gulp and discard liquid Press B to swallow and remove the liquid To pick up water , stand in front of any body of liquid and hold Y while pressing ZR . Ditto will inhale the liquid and hold it. Move to your target location, face the area you want to fill, and press A to release it. info Always build an enclosed pool before spitting out liquid. Any area surrounded by blocks on all sides will contain the liquid neatly. Open terrain will let it spread in unpredictable directions. If you accidentally inhale liquid you do not want to place anywhere, pressing B will make Ditto swallow and permanently discard it. Be careful with this option if your island has limited water sources, since discarded liquid is gone for good. What Liquids Can Suck Move? Suck is not limited to plain water . The full list of transferable liquids in Pokémon Pokopia includes: Water (standard) Ocean water Hot-spring water Vending machine drinks Lava Muddy water This variety opens up a lot of creative possibilities. Moving hot-spring water lets you build custom spa habitats, while relocating lava can help create volcanic terrain features. Why Is the Suck Move Worth the Wait? Unlocking Suck opens up a major layer of island customization that is simply not possible before you have it. Water -type habitats require specific liquid conditions, and being able to relocate water precisely means you can attract Pokémon that would otherwise never appear on your island. Clearing flooded zones also frees up building space that was previously unusable. The progression gate (rebuilding the Rocky Ridges Pokémon Center) takes time, but every step leading up to it also builds out your island in meaningful ways. By the time Paldean Wooper teaches Ditto the move, you will already have a much more developed island to experiment with. For more tips on building habitats, managing island resources, and mastering Ditto 's full move set, browse the latest Pokémon Pokopia guides to keep your island growing.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Bubbly Basin Habitat Warmer Guide
content: Pokémon in the underwater Bubbly Basin area of Pokémon Pokopia have different comfort needs than anything you dealt with on the surface, and one of the first requests you'll run into is a Pokémon asking you to make their home warmer. The solution is simpler than you might expect, but finding the right item does require knowing where to look. What is the best way to warm up a Bubbly Basin habitat? A Heat Rock is the item you need. It radiates heat to the surrounding area, making it the go-to fix for any Pokémon complaining about a cold habitat in Bubbly Basin. Place it in the habitat and the temperature issue resolves. The Heat Rock belongs to a set of four special rocks in Pokémon Pokopia, each designed to modify the local environment in different ways. Loading table... All four are rare items, so you will not stumble across them constantly. The Heat Rock is the one to prioritize for warming up any Bubbly Basin habitat. tip Each special rock affects only the area nearby, so placement matters. Put the Heat Rock directly inside the habitat that needs warming rather than leaving it somewhere else in Bubbly Basin. Bubbly Basin cave entrance Where to find a in Bubbly Basin The most straightforward way to get a Heat Rock is to grab the one sitting inside a Pokéball in a cave within Bubbly Basin. From the gate entrance, head into the main area where Popplio first guides you. Look for a cave on the right side of the stairs — it has black stone above the entrance and scaffolding pieces at the front. Head toward the back of that cave and you will find a Pokéball containing a Heat Rock . That is the one guaranteed spawn, so if you have not collected it yet, that is your fastest route. Heat Rock Pokéball location What are the other ways to get a ? Once you have found your first Heat Rock , there are a couple of ways to get more. 3D Printer : Take a photo of the Heat Rock you already own, then use the 3D Printer to create a duplicate. This costs resources, including Poké Ingots , which are not cheap, so plan accordingly. Cloud Islands: If you have not found the cave Heat Rock yet, some Cloud Islands carry one. Traveling to a Cloud Island that has one lets you collect it without needing the cave first. Gimmighoul and Gholdengo trades: Trading with these two Pokémon can yield a Heat Rock as a reward. The item pool for these trades is broad, though, so this method is not reliable as your primary approach. warning Duplicating items via the 3D Printer requires Poké Ingots, which are a costly resource. Save duplication for items you genuinely need multiples of rather than burning Ingots early. For players managing habitat comfort across multiple Pokémon, knowing how to increase Comfort Level more broadly will help you stay ahead of requests like this one. 3D Printer duplication menu How does the fit into Bubbly Basin habitat management? Bubbly Basin sits underwater, which changes the rules for several comfort mechanics that work fine on the surface. Temperature control through the Heat Rock is one of the adjustments the DLC introduces specifically for this environment. If you are also dealing with humidity-related requests from your Pokémon, the approach there is different. Check out the guide on how to increase humidity in Pokémon Pokopia to handle those separately. For a full picture of every Pokémon available in the expansion, the complete Bubbly Basin DLC Pokémon list covers every confirmed addition and what to expect from Parts 2 and 3. tip The Bubbly Basin location is part of the Expansion Pass Wave 1 content. You need the Expansion Pass active to access this area and its unique habitat mechanics. For everything else the Bubbly Basin expansion adds, the full Pokémon Pokopia guide collection has you covered across habitats, Pokémon spawns, and comfort mechanics.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Hot Spring Shower Psyduck Guide
content: Psyduck is one of the Pokémon players often want to find early in Pokémon Pokopia , but it is not available right away. Unlike some Pokémon that appear naturally during exploration, Psyduck requires a specific habitat setup before it can spawn. This guide explains how to unlock Psyduck , how to build the Hot-Spring Shower habitat , and how to get Hot-Spring Water , which is the key material needed for the environment. When Psyduck Becomes Available Players cannot encounter Psyduck at the very beginning of Pokémon Pokopia. The game first requires progress through the early area of the island. After exploring the first region and unlocking additional building tools and terraforming options, the conditions needed for Psyduck become available. At that point, players can begin building the habitat required to attract it. Psyduck only appears in one specific environment type called the Hot-Spring Shower habitat , which must be created manually. How to Build a Hot-Spring Shower Habitat The Hot-Spring Shower is the only habitat in Pokémon Pokopia that adds Psyduck and Golduck to the Pokémon encounter pool. Psyduck is usually the more common spawn between the two. To create the habitat, players must place the following items together in the same area: One Shower One Seat (any seat works) Two tiles of Hot-Spring Water Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Make a Hot-Spring Shower and Get Psyduck Once these elements are placed close to each other, the environment counts as a Hot-Spring Shower habitat and Psyduck can begin appearing. A simple way to build this setup is inside the Rocky Ridges region. Caves in this area naturally contain Hot-Spring Water, which means players only need to add a Shower and a Seat to complete the habitat. This is usually the fastest method if the goal is to unlock Psyduck quickly. How to Get Hot-Spring Water Hot-Spring Water is one of several liquid types players can place in the environment while terraforming in Pokémon Pokopia. There are two main ways to obtain it. The first method is by collecting natural Hot-Spring Water from areas where it already exists, such as caves in Rocky Ridges. Players can absorb the liquid and place it elsewhere once the proper ability is unlocked. Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Make a Hot-Spring Shower and Get Psyduck The second method involves using an item called Roserade Tea . Roserade Tea can be obtained from a powered Vending Machine . The machine can be used once per day and gives a random item, which may include Fresh Water or Roserade Tea. After drinking Roserade Tea , the player's Ditto temporarily stores liquid. This allows players to place Hot-Spring Water tiles wherever they want, letting them build the Hot-Spring Shower habitat in almost any location. How to Unlock the Liquid Absorb Ability If players want to collect water directly from the environment instead of relying on vending machine items, they must unlock a special ability. This ability comes from Wooper . To start the process, players need to speak with Piplup , who gives a request involving the creation of a Waterfall . Completing this task leads to an interaction with Wooper , which teaches the player how to absorb and store liquids. Once unlocked, this ability greatly expands terraforming options and makes it easier to move Hot-Spring Water from one location to another. Final Tips for Finding Psyduck Once the Hot-Spring Shower habitat is built, Psyduck can begin appearing in the area. If it does not show up immediately, players may need to leave the area and return to refresh Pokémon spawns. Building the habitat in a location that is easy to revisit can make this process faster. Because the habitat also allows Golduck to appear, players can potentially encounter both Pokémon in the same location after the setup is complete.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Pikachu Corner Mimikyu Guide
content: Some Pokémon in Pokémon Pokopia appear naturally while exploring the island, but others only show up after players build very specific habitats. One of the most wanted examples is Mimikyu , the Ghost/Fairy Pokémon that disguises itself as Pikachu. Getting Mimikyu is not complicated, but it requires setting up a special habitat called the Pikachu Corner . This guide explains exactly how to build the habitat and where to find the items needed to unlock it. How to Make a Corner The Pikachu Corner is a simple habitat that attracts only one Pokémon: Mimikyu . No other Pokémon can spawn from it, and Mimikyu will not appear through any other habitat in the game. To create the Pikachu Corner, players only need to place two decorations next to each other: Pikachu Sofa Pikachu Doll Place both items side-by-side in your area. After a short period of time, the environment will trigger the habitat effect and Mimikyu will appear nearby . The build itself is easy. The main challenge is unlocking the two Pikachu -themed items required for the habitat. Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Make a Pikachu Corner and Unlock Mimikyu How to Get the The Pikachu Doll can be purchased later through the Pokémon Center PC once it becomes available, but the fastest way to obtain it is by exploring. Players can find one in the Bleak Beach region. Head toward the southern section of the area where an abandoned house sits on a small island. If the player has already encountered Lapras and unlocked the ability to transform into it, reaching the island becomes much easier. Lapras allows safe travel across the water surrounding Bleak Beach. Without Lapras , it is still possible to reach the island by carefully placing blocks to create a path. However, falling into the water will reset progress, so it requires careful movement. Inside the abandoned house, players will find the Pikachu Doll waiting to be collected. How to Get the The Pikachu Sofa is also located in the Bleak Beach area, but this one is hidden inside the ruins of the S.S. Anne ship. Unlike the Pikachu Doll , this item is much harder to reach without Lapras . The ship is surrounded by water , so transforming into Lapras is strongly recommended before attempting the trip. Once inside the S.S. Anne, explore the upper levels of the ship until reaching the area with the steering wheel . Nearby, there is a ladder positioned above two bookcases. To reach it: Place a block near the bookcases. Jump onto the top of the shelves. Climb the ladder above them. At the top, players will find a glowing yellow Poké Ball containing the Pikachu Sofa . Some later areas in Pokopia also feature a Pikachu Sofa already placed in the environment, but finding the one inside the S.S. Anne is the earliest way to unlock the Pikachu Corner. How to Spawn Once both items are collected, building the habitat is quick. Simply place the Pikachu Sofa and Pikachu Doll next to each other to form the Pikachu Corner . After a short wait, Mimikyu will appear in the area . Because this Pokémon only spawns from this specific habitat, building the Pikachu Corner is the only reliable way to encounter it. For players trying to complete their Pokopia Pokémon collection, setting up this habitat early is the best strategy to secure Mimikyu as soon as possible.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Make Duckweed
content: Duckweed is one of the environmental elements players will need to understand in Pokémon Pokopia . This floating plant grows on water and is required for certain Habitats that attract specific Pokémon. Players who want to complete the Pokopia Pokédex will eventually need to create Duckweed , since some Pokémon only appear in habitats that require it. Learning how to generate it early makes building habitats and unlocking new Pokémon much easier. This guide explains how to make Duckweed in Pokémon Pokopia and whether it can be moved after being placed. How to Make Duckweed In Pokémon Pokopia , Duckweed is created using the Leafage ability while it is powered up. However, Leafage cannot produce Duckweed immediately at the start of the game. The ability first needs to be enhanced by eating a Salad . Players who have not unlocked cooking yet should head to Rocky Ridges and rescue Chef Dente . After helping him, cooking becomes available and salads can be prepared. Once a Salad is eaten, the Leafage PP bar turns yellow , showing that the ability is powered up and has a limited number of enhanced uses. Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Make Duckweed After powering up Leafage, creating Duckweed is easy: Go to any body of water Use the Leafage ability on the water surface Hold the ability button to create a larger Duckweed patch Larger patches of Duckweed will trigger the Uplifting Duckweed Habitat , which allows Pokémon like Lotad and its evolution line to appear. Because of this, many players use Duckweed mainly for habitat creation and Pokémon spawns. Can You Move Duckweed? Currently, Duckweed cannot be moved once it has been placed in Pokémon Pokopia. Abilities that work on other environmental objects do not relocate it: Rototiller does not pick it up Cut only destroys the Duckweed and leaves behind collectible Leaves Because of this limitation, the best approach when building habitats is to create more Duckweed than needed and then trim the extra areas using Cut. Fortunately, most Duckweed -based habitats in the game do not require extremely precise placement, so adjusting the shape is usually enough to complete the setup. Why Duckweed Is Important Duckweed plays a key role in several habitat builds in Pokémon Pokopia. Some Pokémon will only spawn in environments that contain floating foliage, making it necessary for Pokédex completion. Once players unlock cooking, power up Leafage with Salad, and start placing Duckweed in water areas, they can begin unlocking the Uplifting Duckweed Habitat and attract Pokémon such as Lotad, Lombre, and Ludicolo . For players focusing on habitat creation and rare Pokémon spawns, mastering Duckweed placement is an important step in progressing through the game.

title: Pokémon Pokopia: How to Make Lava Pools and Streams
content: Lava is one of the more unique environmental liquids players can work with in Pokémon Pokopia . While Lava naturally appears in certain areas of the map, players can also create their own Lava pools, streams, and waterfalls for custom terrain builds. However, Lava works differently from other liquids in the game. Unlike Hot Spring Water or Muddy Water , it cannot be safely collected directly by jumping into it. Because of that, players need a different method if they want to use Lava for building or terraforming. Here’s how to make Lava in Pokémon Pokopia and how to remove or control it when needed. How to Make Lava in Pokémon Pokopia The easiest and safest way to create Lava is by using Chili Sauce . In Pokémon Pokopia, Ditto can absorb different liquid types. When Ditto consumes Chili Sauce , it temporarily fills with Lava. Players can then place that Lava anywhere in the environment to create custom features like pools, streams, or waterfalls. Pokémon Pokopia: How to Make Lava Pools and Streams The Lava behaves like other liquids in the game and will naturally flow across terrain depending on the layout of the ground. Trying to absorb Lava directly from the environment is not recommended. Jumping into Lava damages Ditto , and repeated attempts will cause the character to respawn nearby. Because of this, Chili Sauce is the intended method for using Lava in builds. How to Get Chili Sauce can be obtained from Vending Machines found around Pokopia. These machines require electricity and will dispense one random item per day when interacted with. Chili Sauce is one of the possible rewards, but the item given is completely random. Since there is no way to guarantee Chili Sauce from a single machine, players should interact with as many Vending Machines as possible each day. Saving the items received can also help build up a supply of liquids for future building projects. How Lava Works When Placed Once Lava is placed in the environment, it behaves like a flowing liquid. This means players can design different terrain features such as: Lava pools Lava streams Lava waterfalls Because Lava flows naturally across terrain, shaping the land beforehand helps control where the Lava spreads. This makes it useful for creating themed areas, especially habitats suited for Fire-type Pokémon , where Lava environments match the overall aesthetic. Can You Move Lava in Pokémon Pokopia? Lava cannot be picked up or moved once it has been placed. Unlike some other liquids in the game, there is no mechanic that allows players to collect placed Lava again. However, it is still possible to remove it from the environment. How to Remove Lava To remove Lava, players need to use Water Spray . Spraying water on Lava converts the liquid into a solid rock block . Once the Lava has turned into rock, it can be destroyed using Rock Smash . This method allows players to clean up mistakes or reshape Lava environments. If the entire Lava area is converted into rock, the Lava will stop appearing in that location. Blocking the Lava source will also prevent it from spreading further. Tips for Building Lava Areas Players who want to build Lava landscapes should prepare the terrain first before placing the liquid. This helps control how far the Lava flows and makes it easier to design streams or pools. Saving Chili Sauce bottles from Vending Machines is also useful since Lava creation depends on having them available. With the right setup, players can design their own volcanic-style zones in Pokémon Pokopia, which work well for Fire-type habitats or themed environments.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Bubbly Basin Unlock Guide
content: The Bubbly Basin DLC is finally live in Pokémon Pokopia , and it brings the first wave of paid Expansion Pass content to the game. Getting in requires a few steps that the game doesn't spell out clearly, so if you've bought the pass and can't figure out why Bubbly Basin isn't showing up yet, here's exactly what you need to do. What are the prerequisites to unlock Bubbly Basin? Bubbly Basin isn't accessible from the start, and the gate won't open until you've met every requirement. Work through this list before expecting anything to happen. Progress requirements You need to have moved past the starting area of the game before Bubbly Basin becomes relevant. Specifically: Complete the Withered Wasteland area, which is where Pokopia begins. Unlock access to Bleak Beach . Finish the 'Raise the Environment Level in Bleak Beach' request. That last one is the gating condition most players miss. You can own the Expansion Pass and have all three movement abilities and still find nothing if that request isn't done. Bleak Beach Pokémon Center Ability requirements Three movement abilities are required to reach and enter Bubbly Basin: Loading table... If you've already raised the Bleak Beach environment level, Jump and Surf are almost certainly already in your toolkit. Dive is the new one added in the v2.0.0 update, and you'll need to learn it from Manaphy specifically. important Dive is the final unlock that triggers Popplio 's appearance. Without it, nothing happens at the Pokémon Center on Bleak Beach. Expansion Pass requirement The Expansion Pass must be purchased. This is the only paid requirement in the list, but it's non-negotiable. Popplio will not appear at Bleak Beach without it , regardless of how far you've progressed in the base game. How to start the Bubbly Basin DLC Once every prerequisite is ticked off, head to the Pokémon Center on Bleak Beach . You'll find Popplio waiting there. Start a conversation with it, and Popplio will talk about its home, then point you toward the gate that leads to Bubbly Basin. The gate itself sits beneath the surface of the sea, parallel to the back of the Pokémon Center. You'll need Dive to reach it, which is why learning the ability from Manaphy first is required. tip If you lose track of where the gate is, talk to Popplio again and it will show you the way. Look for furniture and decorations scattered across the seabed as visual markers pointing toward the entrance. Popplio guides you to the gate Where exactly is the Bubbly Basin gate? The gate is underwater, directly behind the Pokémon Center on Bleak Beach. Dive down from that position and follow the seabed decorations. The layout uses scattered furniture as a breadcrumb trail, so if you see items on the ocean floor, you're heading in the right direction. After testing the path a few times, the most reliable approach is to dive directly behind the center rather than from the sides. The decorations on the seafloor make it hard to get lost once you're in the water . The gate beneath Bleak Beach What's in Bubbly Basin? Bubbly Basin is the first of three content waves included in the Pokémon Pokopia Expansion Pass. It introduces new Pokémon, new areas to build in, and new content tied to the underwater setting. For a full breakdown of every Pokémon confirmed for this wave, check out the complete Bubbly Basin Pokémon list . The DLC launched on August 5, 2026 alongside the v2.0.0 base game update, which also added free content for all players including the Dive ability , Universal Storage , and other changes. Owning the base game gets you those free additions regardless of whether you buy the pass. For more on building out your park once you're in, the full Pokémon Pokopia strategy guides cover habitats, crafting, and Pokémon unlocks across every area of the game.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Dive Ability Unlock Guide
content: The v2.0.0 update for Pokémon Pokopia is the biggest content drop the game has seen, and the Dive ability sits at the center of it. Every player gets access to it, whether or not you have the Expansion Pass, and it opens up underwater building, resource gathering, and exploration in Bleak Beach. Getting there takes a bit of groundwork, though, so here's exactly what you need to do. What are the prerequisites for unlocking Dive? Dive is not something you stumble into early. By the time you can unlock it, you'll have already put a solid chunk of hours into the game. The full list of requirements before you can even start the Dive questline: Complete Withered Wasteland Learn the Jump ability from Magikarp Unlock Bleak Beach Learn the Surf ability from Lapras Complete the 'Raise the Environment Level' request in Bleak Beach All five of these must be done before the Dive chain becomes available. If you're still working through Withered Wasteland or haven't tracked down Lapras yet, Dive is going to stay locked for now. tip The 'Raise the Environment Level' request in Bleak Beach is the gate most players hit last. Focus on building up that area's environment score before expecting Professor Tangrowth to send you anywhere new. Talk to Tangrowth first How to unlock Dive Once all five prerequisites are cleared, head to Bleak Beach and speak to Professor Tangrowth . He'll point you toward a new island in the area. Travel there and talk to Manaphy . Manaphy gives you a request: collect five pieces of Seaweed . The dialogue is a nice touch here. Manaphy acknowledges that you managed to gather them without being able to Dive, which is a small but satisfying acknowledgment of the effort involved. After you hand over the Seaweed, Manaphy teaches you the Dive ability. That's the full sequence: Meet all five prerequisites Speak to Professor Tangrowth in Bleak Beach Travel to the new island he directs you toward Talk to Manaphy Collect 5 Seaweed and return them to Manaphy Receive the Dive ability important You do not need the Expansion Pass to unlock Dive or to use it in Bleak Beach. The DLC expands what Dive can do, but the base ability is free for all players. Collect 5 Seaweed for Manaphy What does Dive actually do? Dive lets you go beneath the water 's surface to explore, collect resources, and build . In Bleak Beach specifically, you can use new crafting items to construct underwater areas, including Pokémon habitats that sit below the waves. The ability gets significantly more mileage if you have the Expansion Pass . Wave 1, which released August 5, 2026, introduces Bubbly Basin , a brand-new underwater environment with new Pokémon and content built entirely around the Dive mechanic. For base-game players, Dive still adds meaningful depth (literally) to Bleak Beach, just without the dedicated new zone. tip If you own the Expansion Pass, completing the Manaphy quest triggers a follow-up task that leads directly into Bubbly Basin. Base-game players still benefit from Dive in Bleak Beach, but the DLC chain won't activate. Build underwater habitats in Bleak Beach What comes next after unlocking Dive? With Dive in hand, Bleak Beach has a lot more to offer. Underwater building opens up new habitat options, and if you're working through the game's Pokémon collection, some species and resources are only accessible beneath the surface. For players who want to get the most out of every ability and Pokémon in the game, our full Pokémon Pokopia strategy guides cover everything from habitat building to ability unlocks. There's also a dedicated breakdown of every Ditto transformation and how to unlock them , which pairs well with this update given the expanded roster of Pokémon now available. If you're still working on earlier island content, the guide on how to unlock the Suck move and move water is worth reading before you start reshaping Bleak Beach's water layout. And if you want a broader look at what makes Pokopia worth your time, check out our full review for the complete picture.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Magnemite Skill Guide: How to Unlock Magnet Rise
content: Ditto gains several skills and transformations throughout Pokémon Pokopia , but players might notice one empty slot still sitting on the skill wheel even after unlocking most abilities. That missing ability is Magnet Rise , the final transformation in the game. Magnet Rise is unlocked in the post-game , and it also turns out to be one of the most useful abilities for building and exploration. This guide explains how to unlock Magnet Rise, how to help Magnemite , and what the ability actually does. How to Unlock Magnet Rise Magnet Rise only becomes available after finishing the main story of Pokémon Pokopia. Once the credits roll and the player loads back into the world, Ditto will return to the same location where the mysterious tower used to stand earlier in the game. After the ending events, the tower is gone and a large hole remains in its place . Pokémon Pokopia Magnemite Skill Guide: How to Unlock Magnet Rise Players may have explored this underground area earlier by entering from the ocean side of the metal structure, but after completing the story something new appears. A Magnemite can now be found there. Talking to Magnemite starts a small quest. It asks the player to build a habitat so it can stay in the area. Completing this request unlocks the final transformation. ’s Habitat To help Magnemite , players must build the Factory Storage habitat . Most of the materials needed for this habitat can be found nearby, which makes the quest fairly quick to complete. The required items are: Jumbled Cords ×1 Streetlight (any type) ×1 Metal Drum ×1 Control Unit ×1 Pokémon Pokopia Magnemite Skill Guide: How to Unlock Magnet Rise The Metal Drum and Jumbled Cords are located close to where the quest begins, so players can collect them immediately. For the Streetlight , any variant works. Many players craft a Mushroom Lamp since it is easy to make and does not require electricity. The last item, the Control Unit , requires a short trip. Players must travel to Sparkling Skylands , specifically the northeast island filled with ruined offices and buildings . A Control Unit can be taken from one of the structures there. After collecting all the parts, return to the Withered Wasteland and place the Factory Storage habitat. Once the habitat is built, speak to Magnemite again to finish the quest. Magnemite then teaches Ditto the Magnet Rise transformation . What Magnet Rise Does Magnet Rise transforms Ditto into Magnemite , giving the player a completely different way to build and interact with the world. While using Magnet Rise, players can freely hover and move in all directions , which makes construction much easier. Instead of jumping around as regular Ditto , players can float around the area while placing blocks and furniture. Pokémon Pokopia Magnemite Skill Guide: How to Unlock Magnet Rise This transformation also acts like an advanced build mode . Players can quickly place structures, reposition objects, and collect materials much faster than normal. Magnet Rise even allows Ditto to absorb certain blocks and materials that could not be picked up before. Because of these advantages, Magnet Rise is widely considered one of the most useful abilities in Pokémon Pokopia, especially for players who enjoy decorating their island or building large structures. Why Magnet Rise Is Worth Unlocking Magnet Rise is the final skill for Ditto and essentially serves as the game’s ultimate building tool . The ability to fly around construction areas, gather blocks efficiently, and place structures quickly makes a huge difference when designing habitats or improving the island. This is also why many players recommend saving large building projects until after finishing the story , since Magnet Rise makes the process significantly easier. Once unlocked, it becomes the best way to shape Pokopia exactly the way players want.

title: Pokemon Pokopia Guide: Hpw to Use Security Cameras
content: Security cameras in Pokemon Pokopia are one of the most practical tools at your disposal, letting you monitor habitats, track Pokemon spawns, and manage your island without running back and forth across the map. If you've been ignoring them, you're making your life a lot harder than it needs to be. How Do You Get Security Cameras in Pokopia? Before placing a single camera, you need to actually own one. Security cameras are available for purchase through the PC's shop , priced at 100 Life Coins each . There's no crafting involved, no quest unlock required. Head to the shop, spend your Life Coins, and you're ready to start building your surveillance network. If you're planning to cover multiple habitats (which you should be), buying several cameras upfront saves you repeated trips back to the shop. Stock up early. Buy security cameras here info Purchase multiple security cameras at once so you can monitor several habitats simultaneously without interrupting your workflow. How to Place and Configure Security Cameras in Pokopia Placement is everything with security cameras. You need to position each camera close to the specific spot you want to monitor, whether that's a habitat, a crop area, or a spawn zone you're watching for a particular Pokemon. Once you've placed a camera, inspect it immediately to check its current view. From the security camera menu , you have three controls available: Angle adjustment to shift the camera's field of view Zoom in to focus on a specific point within the frame Zoom out to capture a wider area Take a moment to fine-tune each camera after placing it. A poorly angled camera that misses the spawn point you're targeting defeats the purpose entirely. danger Position cameras as close as possible to your target area. While the wireless range is generous, closer placement gives you a cleaner, more useful view of the exact spot you're monitoring. Adjust camera angle and zoom How to View Your Security Camera Live Feed Placing cameras is only half the job. Knowing how to access their feeds quickly is what makes the system genuinely useful. Here's the exact process to check your cameras: Open your Pokedex menu Select the Camera app Navigate to the Security Cameras tab Cycle through each camera's live feed if you have multiple placed The ability to cycle through multiple feeds from a single menu means you can survey your entire island in seconds rather than physically traveling to each location. info If you've placed several cameras across different habitats, cycling through feeds in the Security Cameras tab is far faster than fast traveling between locations to check on spawns manually. What Are the Best Uses for Security Cameras in Pokopia? Security cameras shine in a few specific situations. Here's where they add the most value: Use Case Why Cameras Help Tracking rare Pokemon spawns Get notified when a target Pokemon appears in a habitat Monitoring crop and habitat progress Check growth without physically visiting each area Finding undiscovered Pokemon Spot new arrivals passively while doing other tasks Managing large or spread-out islands Reduce travel time across the map significantly Watching specific habitat conditions Confirm environmental requirements are being met The notification system is particularly valuable when you're hunting a specific Pokemon. Rather than repeatedly running to a habitat and finding it empty, cameras alert you when something spawns there, so you can respond at the right moment. Taking Photos Directly From Camera Feeds Beyond monitoring, the security camera menu also lets you take pictures from the camera's perspective. This is useful for documenting Pokemon behavior, capturing habitat shots for reference, or simply getting screenshots from angles you couldn't reach on foot. Building a solid camera network pairs naturally with other island management strategies in Pokopia . If you want to go deeper on habitat mechanics and other systems, browse more guides for additional tips across the game.

title: Pokémon Pokopia Guide: How to Win Hide-and-Sneak
content: Hide-and-Sneak is one of the most tense minigames in Pokémon Pokopia , and it can feel punishing until you understand exactly what you're up against. You have 3 minutes to reach the PC inside the nearby Pokémon Center without getting caught by a group of hunters. Sounds simple. Isn't. Here's everything you need to know to stop losing and start winning consistently. How does Hide-and-Sneak work? The objective is straightforward: touch the PC at the Pokémon Center before the 3-minute timer expires. The obstacle is a group of hunter Pokémon patrolling the area around that same building. Get spotted and caught by any of them, and the round ends. The hunters' positions, patrol directions, and your own starting point shift each round, which means no two attempts play out identically. Zorua is always one of the hunters. The rest are drawn from a random pool each round, so you can't memorize a fixed set of threats from game to game. Spot hunters by their speech bubbles What's the fastest way to reach the PC undetected? The back route is your best friend. Hunters tend to cluster near the front entrance of the Pokémon Center, which makes a direct approach the riskiest path. Circling around to the rear of the building cuts through far less patrolled space and puts you at the PC with much less exposure. Before you move at all, use the Camouflage ability on yourself. Moving through the area in your regular form makes you significantly easier for hunters to spot. Camouflaging immediately after the round begins is one of the highest-impact actions you can take, so don't skip it in the rush to move. tip Camouflage first, move second. Skipping this step is the single most common reason players get caught early. Back route cuts hunter exposure How do you identify which Pokémon are hunters? Hunter Pokémon have speech bubbles floating above their heads. Any Pokémon without a speech bubble is safe to walk past freely. Scan the area in the first few seconds of each round and lock in who's hunting before you commit to a route. Moving without knowing where the hunters are is the fastest way to walk straight into one. Once you've identified the hunters, track their patrol directions as you move. They don't stand still, so a clear path can close off quickly if you're not watching. warning Don't assume last round's hunter positions carry over. The random selection resets every game, so always re-identify hunters from scratch. What should you do when a hunter spots you? When a hunter notices you, a question mark appears above their head and a heartbeat sound plays. The moment either of those signals hits, stop moving completely. Don't take another step. Stay frozen until the hunter turns away and resumes their patrol. Moving even slightly while that question mark is active will confirm their suspicion and end the round. This freeze mechanic is the most reliable escape tool in the game, and it works consistently as long as you react fast enough. Freeze the moment you see this Does placing furniture actually help? Yes, and it's underused. Any furniture or items you place in the playing area before a round starts can serve as cover to hide behind while navigating toward the PC. More objects in the environment means more options to break line of sight with hunters and more surfaces to use as Camouflage anchor points. If you're hitting a wall on a particularly rough run of attempts, stepping back and placing additional items around the field is a legitimate strategy reset. Check out the hidden furniture guide for a full breakdown of every item that can work in your favor here. tip Furniture placement is permanent between rounds, so you only need to set it up once. Arrange it before your first attempt and every subsequent run benefits automatically. Why does luck matter so much? Your starting position and the initial patrol directions of every hunter are randomized at the start of each round. Some configurations are genuinely harder than others, and there's no way to force a favorable layout. The good news is that applying the strategies above makes even difficult configurations manageable, and easier layouts will occasionally just hand you a clean run. The Camouflage approach, back-route preference, and freeze response cover the skill side of the equation. The rest is variance, and variance evens out over enough attempts. What comes after winning Hide-and-Sneak? Once you've secured a win, there's plenty more to dig into. The event tied to this minigame runs until July 27, so time is short if you're chasing the trophy and event rewards. For everything else Pokopia has to offer, the full Pokémon Pokopia strategy guides collection covers every major mechanic and challenge in the game.

title: Dandelion Lunchtime: Jumpluff Habitat & Recruitment Guide
content: Jumpluff , the final evolution of the Hoppip line, is a rare sight in Pokémon Pokopia. While its pre-evolutions are common during the More Spores for Hoppip event , attracting a Jumpluff requires a specific habitat setup and high-tier event items. This guide details the Dandelion Lunchtime recipe, the most effective way to summon Jumpluff to your island. For more general information on how habitats work, check out our Habitat Building Guide . How to Attract Jumpluff Jumpluff can be attracted using two main habitat layouts. While the basic "Yellow Carpet" works for the entire evolutionary line, the Dandelion Lunchtime layout is specifically optimized for Jumpluff. 1. Dandelion Lunchtime (Premium Habitat) This is the recommended setup for trainers specifically hunting for Jumpluff. Filling all four slots of a 2x2 grid with these items significantly increases the spawn rate. A completed 2x2 Dandelion Lunchtime habitat. Required Components: 1x Dandy Flowers 1x Flower Cushion 1x Flowery Table Setting 1x Lunch Box Layout: Place all four items in a 2x2 square anywhere in your main town area. 2. Yellow Carpet (Budget Alternative) If you haven't collected enough spores for the premium items, the Yellow Carpet layout can still attract Jumpluff, though at a much lower frequency compared to Hoppip. Components : 4x Dandy Flowers Layout : Place the 4 flowers in a 2x2 square. Obtaining Materials Most items required for Jumpluff's habitat are exclusive to the More Spores for Hoppip event. Starting the Event According to experts, this event triggers the morning after you successfully rebuild the Pokemon Center in the Withering Wasteland . You will receive a notification that a certain Pokemon is the "talk of the town," signaling that the event has begun. The Event Loop Visit Dream Islands : Use a Doll and find Drifloon to travel to Dream Islands. Collect Cotton Spores : You will need a total of 30 Cotton Spores to purchase the complete Dandelion Lunchtime furniture set. Resource Note : Cotton Spores do not respawn on the same day once collected from a Dream Island. You must wait for the next day to gather more. Exchange at Pokemon Center : Speak to the event Hoppip inside the Withering Wasteland Pokemon Center. Tips for Collecting More Spores To maximize your efficiency during the limited event window, keep these expert tips in mind: Search Everywhere : Spores are hidden in every nook and cranny. Check atop hills, inside cave systems, and even within abandoned buildings on the Dream Islands. Batch Collecting : Hold down the "Y" button to pick up multiple spores and items at once if they are clustered together. Revisit if Needed : While you can only discover one new Dream Island per day , you can revisit that same island as many times as you want within 24 hours to double-check for any missed spores. Event Reward Prioritization While the habitat items are the priority for catching Jumpluff, you can also exchange spores for other rewards. Here is the recommended buy order: Priority Item Name Spore Cost Why It's Useful High Jumpluff Habitat Set 30 Spores Necessary to attract Jumpluff. Medium Dandy Flower Seeds (Extra) 5 Spores Beautify your island and attract more Hoppips. Medium Flower Garland 5 Spores (x10) Useful for crafting other picnic-themed furniture. Low Juice Trio / Lunch Box 5 Spores Purely decorative or minor requests. [!IMPORTANT] The "More Spores for Hoppip" event is limited-time. Ensure you have exchanged your spores for the Flower Cushion and Flowery Table Setting specifically, as these are the hardest to obtain and essential for the Jumpluff-specific recipe. Jumpluff Data & Specialties Once Jumpluff arrives at your habitat, you can befriend it to gain access to its unique island specialties. Specialty 1: Grow : Helps speed up the growth of berry trees and flowers on your island. Specialty 2: Litter : Increases the chances of finding natural materials on the ground. Rarity : ★★★ (Rare) [!TIP] Jumpluff is an excellent early-game companion for automation because its "Grow" specialty significantly reduces the maintenance time for your island's flora.

title: How to Get Lumber Fast in Pokopia (Complete Guide)
content: How to Get Lumber Fast in Pokopia Lumber is one of the most essential resources in the early game of Pokémon Pokopia . You'll need it for everything from building your first habitats to restoring the Withered Wasteland Pokémon Center. While you might occasionally find small wood piles in the overworld, the most efficient way to get Lumber is through the Chop Specialty and the Cut Move . Key Steps to Get Lumber Find Scyther : Build a "Tree-Shaded Tall Grass" habitat. Learn Cut : Complete Scyther's request to learn the move. Collect Small Logs : Use Cut on trees or lumber piles. Process into Lumber : Give Small Logs to a Pokémon with the Chop Specialty . 1. How to Find Scyther Scyther is the first Pokémon you'll encounter that can help you with lumber. To attract one, you need to create its favorite habitat in the Withered Wasteland . Building the Tree-Shaded Tall Grass Habitat Requirements : Place 4 Tall Grass tiles around a Large Tree . Pro-Tips : Use Water Gun to water trees. Use Leafage (Press ZR to switch moves) to create the grass tiles. Wait for the grass to shake, indicating a Pokémon has arrived. 2. Learning the Cut Move Once Scyther appears, talk to it. It will have an orange speech bubble. Request : Scyther wants 2 Sturdy Sticks . Reward : It will teach you the Cut Move . Usage : Press ZR to cycle through your moves until you select Cut. 3. How to Get Small Logs Lumber cannot be gathered directly; you must first gather Small Logs . Where to find : Look for large piles of wood blocking paths around the Pokémon Center ruins. Action : Use your newly learned Cut move on these piles to break them into Small Logs. Warning : You can also cut down trees, but we recommend keeping them for Berries and habitats early on. 4. Processing Small Logs into Lumber This is where the Chop Specialty comes in. Scyther (and later Pokémon like Pinsir) has this ability. The Exchange : 1 Small Log = 5 Lumber . The Process : Give a Small Log to Scyther. It will begin "wailing away" at the log with its blades. Real-Time Crafting : It takes time to process. Since Pokopia uses a real-time clock, you can leave the game or explore, and the Pokémon will finish the job while you're away. Fast Farming Tip : Log in during the morning to hand over your logs, and they'll be ready for your building session in the evening! Lumber Requirements for Main Quests To rebuild the Withered Wasteland Pokémon Center , you will need 10 Lumber . This means you only need to process 2 Small Logs with Scyther's help. Summary Checklist Resource Source Method Small Logs Wood Piles / Trees Use Cut move Lumber Pokémon with Chop Specialty Process Small Logs Sturdy Sticks Ground Spawns Pick up manually Mastering this loop early is the key to mastering Pokopia's building mechanics!

title: Mosslax Guide: Location, Wake Up Quest & Boosts List
content: In Pokémon Pokopia , Mosslax is a unique version of Snorlax that has slept for so long that moss has covered its body. Finding and waking Mosslax is a multi-step journey through Bleak Beach , but the rewards are well worth it. Once awake, Mosslax's Eat specialty provides powerful gameplay boosts that can help you find rare items, attract more Pokémon, or even get discounts at the shop. Where to Find Mosslax You can find Mosslax in Bleak Beach , an area accessible after completing the Withered Wasteland Pokémon Center (past the first encounter with Drilbur ). From the Withered Wasteland entrance, head south toward the abandoned S.S. Anne . Turn left toward the beach hut and the stagnant water wheel. On the cliffside, you'll see several blocks. Use Rock Smash to break through. Mosslax is inside the lair, but it will remain asleep until you complete its specific questline. How to Wake Up Mosslax: "Brighten Things Up!" Waking Mosslax requires restoring light to Bleak Beach through the "Brighten Things Up!" questline. Before starting, ensure you've fixed the Pokémon Center and built habitats for Meowth and Trubbish . Step 1: Follow Trubbish Eventually, Trubbish will hear strange noises. Lead it to Mosslax's location (you may need to build some bridges). Step 2: Harbor Streetlights for Meowth Speak to Meowth in town. It will ask you to craft and place several Harbor Streetlights throughout the town. Use a Pokémon with the Generate specialty (like Pawmi ) to power them. Step 3: Torchic's Resort Habitat Torchic will task you with creating a Resort meal prep habitat . Head to the beach directly in front of Mosslax's lair. You'll find a campfire and palm tree already there. Add: Log Chair Plate Leppa Berry Step 4: Peakychu and the Shell Lamp A new Pokémon, Peakychu ( Pikachu ), will arrive in town. After meeting it, Peakychu will suggest using a Shell Lamp to brighten Mosslax's cave. Recipe : 2x Seashell, 2x Sea glass fragments. Action : Craft the lamp, place it in the cave, and power it with an electric Pokémon. Step 5: Windmill and Utility Poles Peakychu will lead you to the Windmill on the beach. Place a Utility Pole within the Windmill's vicinity to transfer power. Place a Harbor Streetlight next to the Utility Pole. Step 6: The Flash Device Finally, Peakychu will lead you to a device. Clear any blocks in the way. Connect the device to a power source using Utility Poles . Once all five bulbs on the device light up, Peakychu will absorb the energy and perform Flash , illuminating the entire town. Final Step: The Lightning Strike After the town is brightened, return to Mosslax. A final lightning strike from a new Pokémon will hit the cliffside, waking Mosslax and opening up a new path. Mosslax's Specialty: Eat Once befriended, you can utilize Mosslax's specialty, Eat . By offering food at its habitat, the Gourmet's Altar , you receive a special boost that lasts until the end of the in-game day (05:00 local time). Gourmet's Altar Requirements Core : Offering Dish. Item Preferences : Mosslax likes "Strange" and "Soft" items. List of Mosslax Boosts The effect depends on the Dominant Flavor of the food offered. Fully cooked meals (see our Cooking Guide ) provide a significantly stronger boost than raw berries. Dominant Flavor Effect Generic Increased rate of growing closer to Pokémon (Friendship) Bitter Increased chance of finding rare items Dry Increased chance to encounter Pokémon with rare feathers (e.g., Kyogre ?, Lugia, Ho-Oh) Sour 10% Shop Discount + Increased chance of "Good" shop items Spicy Increased chance of Pokémon appearing in habitats Sweet Increased chance of finding Ancient Artefacts tip If you're hunting for Legendaries like Lugia or Ho-Oh, offer Mosslax a Dry flavored meal (like Mushroom Soup) to maximize your chances of seeing rare feathers!

title: Pokemon Pokopia Photo Ops Guide
content: Pokemon Pokopia's camera system is one of its most charming features, but the Highlight Reel takes things beyond casual snapshots. These are scripted, one-time moments between your Pokemon and specific items or each other, and the game rewards you with exclusive photo frames for capturing them. Miss the notification, and that particular shot won't come back. Knowing exactly what to set up, and where, makes all the difference. What are Photo Ops in Pokemon Pokopia? Photo Ops are curated interactions that trigger under specific conditions as you build out your Pokopia community. When one is about to happen, a notification appears in the top right corner of your screen reading "Get your camera! A great photo op is happening nearby!" Press the - button on your left Joy-Con to pull out the camera immediately. Once the camera is open, follow the on-screen arrows toward the interaction. A border will appear around the Pokemon at the center of the moment. Take the shot using the in-game camera (not your Switch's screenshot button), and if the framing is correct, the photo op title flashes on screen and the image gets filed into your Highlight Reel under the Collections menu ( + button, then the Collection treasure chest). warning Using your Switch's built-in screenshot feature instead of the in-game camera will NOT register the photo op. Always use the in-game camera. Each Photo Op only triggers once. After you capture it, that specific scripted moment won't repeat, though you can still photograph your Pokemon freely at any time. Photo op alert notification How do you increase your chances of triggering Photo Ops? You cannot force most Photo Ops to fire on demand, but you can stack the odds in your favor. The key is placing the relevant items throughout your habitats before the notification has any chance to appear. A campfire sitting in a Pokemon's habitat is far more likely to produce the "Toasty Warm by the Campfire " moment than one you haven't placed yet. info Place multiple copies of key items like campfires, perches, and hot springs across different habitats. More exposure means more chances for the notification to fire. All Photo Ops and their requirements The table below covers every confirmed Photo Op in the Highlight Reel, what you need to trigger it, and any rewards it unlocks. Photo Op Requirement Reward Toasty Warm by the Campfire Any Pokemon relaxing near a Campfire Fire Spin Photo Frame A Gust of Wind to Get It Spinning Any Flying-type Pokemon spinning a Pinwheel with its wings None confirmed Punching Past the Sound Barrier Hitmonchan using a Punching Bag Impact Photo Frame Spacious Slumber Party Multiple Pokemon napping together (bench or large bed helps) None confirmed Greetings from Beyond the Grave A Ghost-type Pokemon interacting with a Gravestone Mysterious Frame Fun in the Sand Any Pokemon playing in a Sandbox Dust Cloud Photo Frame Found Some Delicious... Trash? Trubbish nibbling on Trash None confirmed Nothing Like a Quick Dip! Any Pokemon using a Sprinkler or Shower Bubble Photo Frame Stacking Blocks, Psychic Style A Psychic-type Pokemon playing with Wooden Toy Blocks None confirmed Battin' Around the Old Yarn Meowth playing with Knitting Supplies None confirmed A Cool, Gentle Breeze Any Pokemon interacting with a Fan None confirmed Roost and Rest A Flying-type Pokemon napping on a Perch None confirmed This Is the Life Any Pokemon soaking in a Hot Spring None confirmed Sweet Dreams with a Mossy Pillow Any Pokemon napping on Moss or near a mossy rock None confirmed Open It Up, and— Boo! Any Pokemon playing with the Boo-in-the-Box Lost Relic (L) Keep Out Photo Frame Martial Arts Training Montage Two Fighting-type Pokemon ( Hitmonchan , Hitmonlee , or Hitmontop ) sparring None confirmed The Skyland Specialists Tinkmaster and Conkeldurr interacting None confirmed No, My Horns Are Better! Heracross and Pinsir arguing near Graveler None confirmed Step Right Up, Step Right Up! A Pokemon with the Trade specialty at a Register None confirmed A Hypnotizing Lullaby Jigglypuff singing on a stage None confirmed A Cook's Gotta Eat Too! Chef Dente enjoying a meal (triggers at Rocky Ridges party if missed) None confirmed A Head Full of Blooming Flowers Mosslax's flowers blooming (only after completing Bleak Beach) None confirmed DJ Droppin' the Beats! DJ Rotom playing music for another Pokemon None confirmed Photo Ops that need specific setup Some of these won't happen organically without deliberate preparation. Here are the ones worth planning around: Open It Up, and— Boo! This one requires the Boo-in-the-Box , a Lost Relic item classified as size (L). You need to find it first, then place it somewhere your Pokemon can reach and interact with it. The payoff is worth the effort: Vespiquen getting startled by a Gengar popping out is genuinely one of the funnier moments in the game, and it unlocks the Keep Out Photo Frame . Greetings from Beyond the Grave You need a Gravestone item placed in a habitat where Ghost-type Pokemon live. Gastly is confirmed to trigger this one. If you haven't built a Ghost-type habitat yet, this won't fire naturally. Highlight Reel collection album No, My Horns Are Better! This requires both Heracross and Pinsir to be living in your Pokopia simultaneously. Both need to be in a position where they can interact with each other, and the game uses Graveler as a prop in their argument. Make sure both are housed before expecting this notification. A Head Full of Blooming Flowers This is story-locked. You cannot access this Photo Op until after completing the Bleak Beach storyline . Once that's done, Mosslax's flowers will eventually bloom and trigger the notification. How to view your completed Highlight Reel All captured Photo Ops are stored in the Highlight Reel section of your Collections menu. Press + to open the main menu, select the Collection treasure chest, then navigate to the Highlight Reel tab. Every photo taken through a Photo Op notification will have a pink camera icon in the bottom-left corner to distinguish it from regular snapshots. Your in-game photo album does have a storage limit, but any photo can be exported directly to your Nintendo Switch's system gallery from within the album. This means you can clear space without losing your Highlight Reel shots permanently. Tips for completing the full Highlight Reel faster Build diverse habitats early. The more varied your Pokemon housing, the more interactions you'll see. Campfires, perches, hot springs, and sprinklers should go in early. Don't ignore Lost Relics. The Boo-in-the-Box is a Lost Relic (L), meaning it's found out in the world rather than crafted. Keep an eye out for it during exploration. House rival Pokemon together. Heracross and Pinsir , Hitmonchan and Hitmonlee , Tinkmaster and Conkeldurr : these pairs need to coexist in your community to trigger their respective moments. Complete story beats. Bleak Beach and Rocky Ridges both gate specific Photo Ops. Progressing the main story unlocks them. Check your Highlight Reel regularly. Seeing what's already captured helps you identify gaps and figure out which items or Pokemon you're still missing. For a deeper look at building the right habitats to support these interactions, the Photo Ops guide on IGN) covers confirmed examples for several of the trickier shots. You can also find more Pokemon Pokopia tips and other gaming guides at GAMESgg .

title: Pokopia Shiny Hunting Guide (2026): Are There Shinies or Unique Variants?
content: Pokémon Pokopia Shiny Guide TL;DR Pokopia currently does not use the classic random shiny system seen in mainline games. Instead, the game focuses on unique one-per-species identities and special event or story variants. If you are hunting "rare-looking" Pokemon, your best path is to follow event updates, complete request chains, and improve your habitat progression instead of resetting for odds. Treat this page as your decision shortcut: if your goal is collection value, prioritize event schedules, request rewards, and comfort/habitat milestones before spending time on traditional shiny methods. For many veteran Trainers, Shiny Hunting is the ultimate endgame. However, Pokémon Pokopia handles things a bit differently than traditional entries like Pokémon Scarlet & Violet or Pokémon Legends: Arceus . If you're looking for those elusive sparkling variants, here is the current state of Shiny Pokémon in Pokopia. Can You Find Shiny Pokémon in Pokopia? As of the current version, traditional Shiny Pokémon (random color variants with sparkles) do not appear in the wild. Why the Change? Unlike mainline games where you can catch hundreds of the same species, Pokopia is built on the concept of Unique Identities . There is only one Bulbasaur, one Scyther, and one Pikachu in your game world. Since each Pokémon is a unique individual with its own role in your ranch, the game does not support the "random spawn" mechanic required for traditional shiny hunting. Special "Unique" Pokémon While you won't find a "Shiny" in the traditional sense, Pokopia features Unique NPC Pokémon that stand out from their species with special designs, accessories, or alternate color palettes. Professor Tangrowth A perfect example is Professor Tangrowth . Appearance : Features a white "hair" top that makes it look like a distinguished scholar. Status : While it looks like a rare variant, it is a unique story-driven NPC rather than a random shiny spawn. Event-Exclusive Pokémon Keep an eye out for seasonal events! Most "Special" versions of Pokémon in Pokopia are tied to: Story Requests : Completing Important Requests for certain NPCs. Environment Milestones : Reaching high Environment or Comfort levels. Limited-Time Events : Such as the upcoming Hoppip event. Bubbly Basin DLC & New Pokémon The Bubbly Basin DLC (released August 5, 2026) introduces 50 new Water-type Pokémon to Pokopia. These Pokémon follow the same one-per-species rule as the base game. See the Bubbly Basin DLC Guide for details. There's also an upcoming Fetching Scales for Feebas event (August 13–28, 2026) bringing Feebas and Milotic to the Bubbly Basin. Will Shiny Hunting Be Added? The gaming community (including TheGamer and VGC ) is keeping a close watch. While the one-per-species rule makes random hunting difficult, there are theories about future updates: Costumes/Skins : Using items to change the "color" of your existing Pokémon. Dream Islands / Bubbly Basin : The Bubbly Basin DLC area introduces underwater exploration where non-unique Pokémon behavior may differ. Related Guides Pokopia Habitats Guide Pokopia Best Builds Guide Pokopia Game Length Guide FAQ Does Pokopia have real shiny odds like 1/4096? No. As of now, Pokopia does not run the standard random shiny odds system used in mainline Pokemon titles. Why do some Pokemon look different in screenshots? Those are usually special NPC or event variants, not random shiny spawns from repeated encounters. What should I farm instead of shiny encounters? Prioritize request progression, habitat upgrades, and event participation to unlock rare companions and unique visuals. Summary for Collectors Feature Traditional Games Pokémon Pokopia Shiny Odds 1/4096 (Base) N/A Hunting Method Masuda Method / Outbreaks N/A Special Variants Shiny Palettes Unique NPC Designs & Accessories Recruitment Catching Habitat Building & Requests Final Verdict : If you see a Pokémon that looks "different" in Pokopia, it's likely a Special Unique NPC or an Event Reward ! Cherish your unique partners, as there is literally no one else like them in your world.

title: How to Get Smooth Rock and Create Onix Habitat in Pokopia
content: In Pokémon Pokopia , building the Smooth Tall Grass Habitat for Onix during the "Yawn Up A Storm" quest is one of the first major hurdles for trainers. Finding the Smooth Rock and understanding the unique mechanics of gathering Dry Tall Grass are key to completing the request. This guide provides the exact location of the Smooth Rock and the specific steps to restore Onix's favorite habitat. How to get Smooth Rock in Pokopia The Smooth Rock is located inside the same cave where you first encounter and rescue Onix in the Withered Wasteland area. Precise Location Head back to the cave in the northwest corner of the Withered Wasteland . As you navigate deep into the cave (near where Onix was trapped), look toward the left side of the path. You will spot a red Poké Ball item pickup sitting on a shelf-like rock formation. Interact with the Poké Ball to collect the Smooth Rock . Visual Guide: The item pickup spot inside Onix's cave (Credit: Radio Times). [!NOTE] You do not need to craft or purchase the Smooth Rock. It is a one-time world item pickup essential for this quest. How to make Dry Tall Grass The most confusing part of the habitat recipe is obtaining Dry Tall Grass . Unlike regular grass, this item cannot be bought or crafted; it must be harvested using a specific Pokémon skill. The Leafage Trick Find a patch of Tall Grass on dry ground (ground that has NOT been watered). Use the move Leafage directly on the dry grass patch. The grass will transform into Dry Tall Grass , which you can then collect. Building the Smooth Tall Grass Habitat Once you have 1x Smooth Rock and 4x Dry Tall Grass , you are ready to assemble the habitat. Installation Layout Place the 4x Dry Tall Grass in a 2x2 square grid on the ground. Place the Smooth Rock immediately next to the 2x2 square. Layout: The correct 2x2 arrangement for the Onix habitat (Credit: Radio Times). When the arrangement is correct, a notification will appear confirming that the Smooth Tall Grass Habitat has been restored. You can then speak to Onix to finish the quest!
